'''Sandra Gail Biedron''' (born 1973) is an American [[physicist]] who serves as the Director of Knowledge Transfer for the Center for Bright Beams<ref name="auto">{{cite web|title=The Center for Bright Beams|url=https://cbb.cornell.edu|language=en}}</ref> as well as professor in Electrical & Computer Engineering<ref>{{Cite web|title=Electrical and Computer Engineering UNM|url=https://ece.unm.edu/faculty-staff/research-faculty-profiles/index.html|language=en-us}}</ref> and Mechanical Engineering at the [[University of New Mexico]], where in 2021 she mentors nine graduate students and two post-doctoral researchers. Her research includes developing, controlling, operating, and using laser and particle accelerator systems. She is also Chief Scientist of Element Aero,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Element Aero|url=http://www.elementaero.com/|language=en-us}}</ref> a consulting and R&D company incorporated in 2002. She was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2013.

== Early life and education ==
Biedron grew up in [[Palos Park, Illinois]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=DeGrane|first=Susan|title=Beverly scientist plays key role in fight against coronavirus, gender discrimination in STEM fields|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/daily-southtown/ct-sta-beverly-scientist-coronavirus-st-0327-20200328-rbyj2titofdepjulhnihppq7pa-story.html|access-date=2021-04-10|website=chicagotribune.com|date=28 March 2020 }}</ref> Her father, Emil John Biedron, was a data scientist and engineer who calculated the re-entry trajectories for space shuttle missions.<ref name=":0" /> Her mother, Gail Jean Biedron, encouraged her early interest in chemistry, biology, and antiquity.<ref name=":0" /> She lived on a 7-acre property and spent her childhood riding horses.<ref name=":0" /> She attended [[Carl Sandburg High School]].<ref name=":0" />

Biedron started her academic career at a [[Community colleges in the United States|community college]]: she was a student at [[Moraine Valley Community College]], where she completed her classes in 1992 before moving to [[Trinity Christian College]] in [[Palos Heights, Illinois]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Sandra Biedron Inducted into Moraine Valley Alumni Hall of Fame|url=https://www.morainevalley.edu/news-story/sandra-biedron-inducted-into-moraine-valley-alumni-hall-of-fame/|access-date=2021-04-10|website=Moraine Valley Community College|date=28 February 2020 |language=en-us}}</ref> where she majored in chemistry and biology. Biedron was often in [[Sweden]] for her graduate studies at [[Lund University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Faculty Profile – Electrical and Computer Engineering – College of Engineering – Colorado State University|url=https://www.engr.colostate.edu/ece/facultystaff/facultypage.php?pass=106|access-date=2021-04-10|website=www.engr.colostate.edu}}</ref>

Her dissertation was in [[accelerator physics]] with an emphasis on the generation of coherent, laser-like light sources often known as [[free-electron laser]].<ref>{{cite thesis|title=Toward Creating a Coherent, Next-Generation Light Source with special emphasis on nonlinear harmonic generation in single-pass, high-gain free-electron lasers|first=Sandra|last=Biedron|type=PhD|publisher=[[Lund University]]|date=14 December 2001|url=https://lup.lub.lu.se/search/publication/42149}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
In 1993, Biedron joined the [[Argonne National Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" /> Her research includes the development of coherent, laser-like light sources.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Today @ Colorado State University – Engineering Professor Sandra Biedron elected SPIE Fellow|url=https://today-archive.colostate.edu/story1f2e.html?id=6653|access-date=2021-04-10|website=today-archive.colostate.edu|archive-date=2021-04-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410212402/https://today-archive.colostate.edu/story1f2e.html?id=6653}}</ref> Biedron was eventually appointed as an Associate Director of the Argonne Accelerator Institute and the Department of Defense Project Office.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wpafb.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/401338/afrl-pens-agreement-with-does-argonne-national-lab/https://www.wpafb.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/401338/afrl-pens-agreement-with-does-argonne-national-lab/|title=AFRL pens agreement with DOE's Argonne National Lab|website=Wright-Patterson AFB}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> At Argonne, Biedron helped to develop the [[self-amplified spontaneous emission]] [[free-electron laser]] in the visible wavelengths as well as the [[Advanced Photon Source]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Dr.Sandra Biedron|url=http://221.143.46.125/20special/pleanary%20speaker2.htm|access-date=2021-04-10|website=221.143.46.125}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> She also oversaw and participated in experiments in high-gain harmonic generation free-electron lasers <ref name=":3" /> at the [[Accelerator Test Facility (New York)|Accelerator Test Facility]] at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. She worked on the [[Office of Naval Research]] [[free-electron laser]] and the FERMI@ELETTRA<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fermi@Elettra FEL|url=https://www.elettra.trieste.it/lightsources/fermi.html|language=en}}</ref> [[free-electron laser]] at [[Elettra Sincrotrone Trieste]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Sandra Biedron – CSU Accelerator Laboratory|url=https://projects-web.engr.colostate.edu/accelerator/profile.php?profile=SandraBiedron|access-date=2021-04-10|website=projects-web.engr.colostate.edu}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Sandra Gail Biedron – 2008 SPIE Women in Optics Planner|url=https://spie.org/about-spie/advocacy/women-in-optics/women-in-optics-planner/2008-wio-planner/biedron-sandra-gail|access-date=2021-04-10|website=spie.org}}</ref>

Biedron's work on the high-gain harmonic generation free-electron lasers and other coherent devices<ref>{{cite web |url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US6831933 |title=Modular approach to the next generation, short wavelength, laser-like light sources |last= Patent no. 6831933}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Overview of FERMI@ELETTRA a Proposed Ultra Bright Coherent X-ray Source in Italy |last=Bocchetta|first=C.J. ... |journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment |date=2003 |volume=507 |issue=1–2 |publisher=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment 507 |pages= 484–488|doi=10.1016/S0168-9002(03)00901-X |bibcode=2003NIMPA.507..484B }}</ref> helped drive the FERMI free electron laser at [[ELETTRA]]<ref>{{cite journal |title=Highly coherent and stable pulses from the FERMI seeded free-electron laser in the extreme ultraviolet |last=Allaria |first=E. |journal=Nature Photonics |date=2012 |volume=6 |issue=10 |pages=699–704|doi=10.1038/nphoton.2012.233 |bibcode=2012NaPho...6..699A |s2cid=120228185 }}</ref> and other machine architectures.

Biedron moved to [[Colorado State University]] in 2011.<ref name=":2" /> In 2017, Biedron moved to the [[University of New Mexico]], where she is involved with expanding reach in applied electromagnetism and accelerator technologies.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=Engineering professor receives IEEE Particle Accelerator Science and Technology Award :: School of Engineering {{!}} The University of New Mexico|url=https://engineering.unm.edu/news/2017/11/engineering-professor-receives-ieee-particle-accelerator-science-and-technology-award.html|access-date=2021-04-10|website=engineering.unm.edu}}</ref> She also serves as the Director of Knowledge Transfer at the Center for Bright Beams.<ref name="auto"/>

Her research interests include energy-relevant systems (particle accelerator systems, laser systems, and their application for materials), the use of artificial intelligence in controls, modeling, and prediction of complex systems, including for quantum information systems, sensors and detectors, and applications of these technologies in science, security, and defense. Biedron is active in global security concerns, including dual-use technologies.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Summary Report – International FEL Expert Meeting: "Use of free-electron lasers and beyond: Scientific, technological, and legal aspects of dual use in international scientific cooperation" system|year=2020 |publisher=European XFEL |url=https://xfel.tind.io/record/2268|language=en}}</ref> In September 2021, she addressed artificial intelligence and machine learning for the control of complex systems in the [[Electric Power Research Institute]]'s AI and electric power summit.<ref>{{Cite web|title=EPRI's AI and electric power summit|url= https://www.aielectricpower.com|language=en}}</ref> On 28 September 2021, the U.S. patent number 11,131,106 was awarded to Biedron for construction equipment for use on devices such as radio-frequency (RF) "radio" towers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Containment shroud system|url=https://www.patentguru.com/US11131106B2|language=en}}</ref> Biedron is active in the LANL experiment CCM (Coherent Captain Mills)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Coherent Captain Mills|url= https://p25ext.lanl.gov/~lee/CaptainMills/|language=en}}</ref> at the Lujan center to search for sterile neutrinos, dark matter and axions.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=First dark matter search results from Coherent CAPTAIN-Mills|year= 2022|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevD.106.012001|arxiv= 2105.14020|language=en|last1= Aguilar-Arevalo|first1= A. In 2022, Biedron gave a talk, "Accelerator Development for Global Security", at the XXXI International Linear Accelerator Conference,<ref>{{cite web|title=The 2022 International Linear Accelerator Conference|url=https://linac2022.org|language=en}}</ref> Liverpool, UK. Also in 2022, Biedron served as an invited speaker and panel member at two events – at the Sustainability Summit at SEMICON West (San Francisco, California, 13 July 2022) <ref>{{cite web|title=Sustainability Summit at SEMICON West|url=https://www.semiconwest.org/programs/sustainability-summit|language=en}}</ref> "Opportunity to Innovate: Five Opportunities for Collaborative Innovation for Decarbonized Discovery, Innovation, Design and Manufacturing," <ref>{{cite web|title=Sustainability Summit Keynotes|url=https://www.eventscribe.net/2022/SEMI/SearchByBucket.asp?f=PresentationSessionType&bm=Sustainability&pfp=SustainabilitySummit|language=en|date=July 13, 2022|access-date=September 29, 2022}}</ref>
and at the International Particle Accelerator Conference, Bangkok, Thailand, 15 June 2022  <ref>{{cite web|title=The 2022 International Particle Accelerator Conference|url=https://www.ipac22.org|language=en}}</ref> "Present status and opportunities for implementing disruptive technologies arising in particle accelerator R&D industrial market.".<ref>{{cite web|title=Proceedings of the 13th International Particle Accelerator Conference|url=https://accelconf.web.cern.ch/ipac2022/|language=en|access-date=September 29, 2022}}</ref>

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[Advanced Photon Source]] developed by Biedron and co-workers was used to analyze and generate a detailed model of the [[SARS-CoV-2]] virus.<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Biedron is married to [[Stephen Val Milton]], with whom she has one son Sebastian Milton.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Public Events|url=http://www.ingersoll-blackwelderhouse.com/public-events.html|access-date=2021-04-10|website=Ingersoll-Blackwelder House|language=en}}</ref> She is interested in architecture and since 2014 has owned the Ingersoll-Blackwelder House at 10910 [[South Prospect Street Historic District|S. Prospect]] in [[Chicago]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|title=Press Release|url=http://www.ingersoll-blackwelderhouse.com/press-release.html|access-date=2021-04-10|website=Ingersoll-Blackwelder House|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-08-14|title=Historic Home Welcomes Teen Filmmakers|url=https://bapa.org/historic-home-welcomes-teen-filmmakers/|access-date=2021-04-10|website=Beverly Area Planning Association|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last= Sinkevitch|first=Alice|date=1993 |title= AIA Guide to Chicago, American Institute of Architects|publisher=University of Illinois Press |pages= 470–472}}</ref> Biedron continues to oversee the restoration of the property. It was once owned by a community activity who was the first woman to cast a vote in [[Cook County, Illinois]].<ref name=":7" /> Alongside her historic house, Biedron owns two vintage sports cars and a [[Diamond DA40 Diamond Star]] aircraft.<ref name=":0" /> She is involved with the curation of the steamer trunks and monogrammed linens that were brought by [[Enrico Fermi]] and his family on the voyage on the Cunard Line's RMS Franconia when they fled Europe to avoid [[Fascist Italy (1922–1943)|Fascist Italy]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Stuewer|first=Roger H. |title=Bringing the News of Fission to America |journal=Physics Today |date=1985 |volume=38 |issue=10 |pages=48–56 |publisher=Physics Today 38 |doi=10.1063/1.881016 |bibcode=1985PhT....38j..48S }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Fermi|first=Laura |date=1954 |title=My Life with Enrico Fermi |url= |location=Chicago |publisher=University of Chicago Press |page=139 |isbn=}}</ref>

Biedron serves as a trustee of the [[National Museum of Nuclear Science and History]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=National Museum of Nuclear Science and History Board of Trustees|url=https://www.nuclearmuseum.org/connect/board-of-trustees|language=en}}</ref> Based on her efforts in preservation including architecture, she was admitted to the [[Cliff Dwellers Club]] of Chicago dedicated to people supporting the arts.
